metadata.title: Cloud Cybersecurity Controls (CCC – 2: 2024)
metadata.description: A cloud cybersecurity controls document issued under the National Cybersecurity Authority of Saudi Arabia. It defines controls for Cloud Service Providers (CSPs) and Cloud Service Tenants (CSTs), including objectives, requirements, applicability information, terminology, and updates from the previous CCC – 1: 2020 version. The document is classified as Public under the Traffic Light Protocol (TLP: White).
metadata.hierarchy_description: The document is organized into main domains, subdomains, main controls, and subcontrols. It distinguishes requirements applicable to CSPs and CSTs and uses control identifiers such as 1-1-P-1 and 1-1-T-1. The identified content includes domains covering cybersecurity governance and responsibilities, asset management, identity and access management, network security, mobile device security, data and information protection, cryptography, backup and recovery, vulnerabilities, physical security, web application security, key management, system development security, storage media security, cybersecurity events and incidents, and third-party cybersecurity. The document also includes objectives, a statement of applicability, control-component illustrations, identification notation, and terms and definitions.

source_reference.source_text: The CCC aims to set the minimum requirements for cybersecurity of cloud computing, for both CSPs and CSTs, to contribute to enable the CSPs and the CSTs to provide and use secure cloud computing services and mitigating cyber risks against them. The cybersecurity of cloud computing services, for both CSPs and CSTs, must be able to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data and information within the cloud environment.

todo.name: Implement minimum cloud cybersecurity protections
todo.description: Assess cloud services against the CCC minimum requirements and implement safeguards that protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of cloud data and information.

source_reference.source_text: The cloud cybersecurity controls shall apply to the CSPs and CSTs. These controls represent the minimum cybersecurity requirements for cloud computing. CSPs within the scope of CCC are any CSP which provides cloud computing services to the CSTs within the scope of work. CSTs within the scope of CCC are any government agency in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia inside or outside the Kingdom, including ministries, authorities, establishments and other entities and their companies and sub-entities, as well as all private sector entities owning, operating or hosting Critical National Infrastructures (CNIs) that currently use or are planning to use any cloud service. Every CSP and CST must comply with all applicable controls.

todo.name: Determine CCC scope and applicable controls
todo.description: Classify the organization as a CSP or CST, determine whether it falls within the stated scope, identify every applicable CCC control, and establish a compliance plan for those controls.

source_reference.source_text: The cybersecurity risk management methodology shall include, at minimum, for the CSP: defining acceptable risk levels for the cloud services and clarifying them to the CST if they are related to the CST; considering data and information classification; and developing a cybersecurity risk register for cloud services and monitoring it periodically according to the risks. For the CST, the methodology shall include, at minimum: defining acceptable risk levels for the cloud services; considering data and information classification accredited by the CST; and developing a cybersecurity risk register for cloud services and monitoring it periodically according to the risks.

source_reference.source_text: Positions of cybersecurity functions in CSP data centers within the Kingdom must be filled with qualified and suitable Saudi nationals. Personnel with access to the Cloud Technology Stack shall be screened or vetted periodically. Cybersecurity policies are a prerequisite to access and must be signed and appropriately approved. Entity assets shall be accounted for and returned upon termination.

The CST shall protect the connection channel with the CSP.

source_reference.source_text: The CSP shall secure access, storage, and transfer of CST data backups and Cloud Technology Stack backups and their media against damage, amendment, or unauthorized access. The CSP shall assess and remediate external Cloud Technology Stack vulnerabilities at least monthly and internal components at least every three months, notify CSTs of vulnerabilities that may affect them, and manage notified safeguards. The CST shall assess and remediate cloud-service vulnerabilities at least every three months.

source_reference.source_text: The scope of CSP penetration tests must cover the Cloud Technology Stack and be conducted at least once every six months. CSPs shall activate and protect Cloud Technology Stack event logs and audit trails, collect login history, protect tenant-level activity logs, use SIEM for continuous monitoring of the full stack, periodically review logs, automatically monitor remote-access sessions, and securely handle user-related log data. CSTs shall activate and collect login and cybersecurity event logs and monitor all activated cloud-service logs.

todo.name: Implement penetration testing and cloud security monitoring
todo.description: Schedule stack-wide penetration tests every six months, centralize and protect required logs, enable continuous SIEM monitoring, review logs periodically, monitor remote sessions, and ensure CST cloud-service logging and monitoring.

source_reference.source_text: CSP system-development cybersecurity requirements shall be identified, documented, approved, applied, and periodically reviewed. They shall address Cloud Technology Stack and relevant system requirements in design and implementation, and protection of development, testing, and integration environments. CSP media controls shall require sanitization before disposal or reuse, secure disposal, confidentiality and integrity of removable-media data, human-readable classification labels, controlled secure storage, and restricted portable-media use.

todo.name: Secure development and storage media handling
